# Command Systems: The "Cmd+K" Power User Experience

In a typical web app, you navigate by clicking buttons. In a **Pro Tool**, you navigate by thinking.

Apps like VS Code, Linear, and Notion have trained users to expect a global "Command Palette" (`Cmd+K` or `Ctrl+K`). This chapter shows you how to build one in React.

---

## 1. The Command Pattern

The "Command Pattern" separates the *intent* from the *execution*.

```ts
type Command = {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  icon?: React.ReactNode;
  perform: () => void;
};
```

Instead of burying logic in a button's `onClick`, you register commands in a central registry.

---

## 2. Using `cmdk`

Don't build the UI from scratch. The library `cmdk` (by Pace) is the gold standard. It handles the accessible dialog, filtering, and keyboard navigation.

```bash
npm install cmdk
```

```tsx
import { Command } from 'cmdk';
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';

export function CommandPalette() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

  // Toggle with Cmd+K
  useEffect(() => {
    const down = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (e.key === 'k' && (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey)) {
        e.preventDefault();
        setOpen((open) => !open);
      }
    };
    document.addEventListener('keydown', down);
    return () => document.removeEventListener('keydown', down);
  }, []);

  return (
    <Command.Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
      <Command.Input placeholder="Type a command or search..." />

      <Command.List>
        <Command.Empty>No results found.</Command.Empty>

        <Command.Group heading="Projects">
          <Command.Item onSelect={() => console.log('Create Project')}>
            Create New Project
          </Command.Item>
          <Command.Item onSelect={() => console.log('Search Projects')}>
            Search Projects...
          </Command.Item>
        </Command.Group>

        <Command.Group heading="Settings">
          <Command.Item onSelect={() => console.log('Toggle Theme')}>
            Toggle Dark Mode
          </Command.Item>
        </Command.Group>
      </Command.List>
    </Command.Dialog>
  );
}
```

---

## 3. Global Shortcuts

`Cmd+K` is just the entry point. You also want shortcuts like `Cmd+S` (Save) or `Cmd+B` (Toggle Sidebar).

Use a custom hook `useKeyboardShortcut`:

```tsx
import { useEffect } from 'react';

function useKeyboardShortcut(key: string, callback: () => void, meta = false) {
  useEffect(() => {
    const handler = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (event.key === key && event.metaKey === meta) {
        event.preventDefault();
        callback();
      }
    };
    window.addEventListener('keydown', handler);
    return () => window.removeEventListener('keydown', handler);
  }, [key, callback, meta]);
}

// Usage
function App() {
  useKeyboardShortcut('s', () => saveProject(), true); // Cmd+S
  return <div>App</div>;
}
```

By decoupling input (Keyboard/Mouse) from actions (Commands), you make your app scriptable, testable, and incredibly fast to use.
